renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Minds unawake, keen to hide their own stand — they knock folk down on the hard road, terrible to cross. So always trying to tell stirring-truth apart: awake indeed, they soon reach their own state. Angry, thrilled, wondering what to do, running — whichever step it takes, there stirring stands.
Which state grabbed, whatever this tells me — that I will do: so decided, he stands. Her, by the upper road, moon and sun both — set in the middle channel, past the egg of the world.
Then in that huge sky, moon and sun gone — like deep sleep: fooled or awake, all may stand uncovered.

paragraphs.text: Unwoke minds, busy hiding their own stand — knocking people down on the hard road, terrible crossing. So always grinding to split stirring-truth: awake for real, own state unlocked soon. Mad, hyped, what-do-I-do, running — whatever step, stirring posted up there.
State grabbed, orders received — that I will do: decided, standing. Her, up the high road, sun and moon both — parked in the middle channel, past the world-egg.
Then in that big sky, sun and moon dissolved — deep-sleep mode: fooled or woke, all uncovered.
